name: OpenVibe.Events
tagline: Events, queues and webhooks you can build on.
description: OpenVibe.Events is the network's event system: durable events, topics and subscriptions, signed webhooks with retries, dead-letter queues and replay, pull consumers with checkpoints, and realtime delivery to browsers with cursor resume. Every OpenVibe product already publishes through it. This domain is its home: the developer docs, the API and the realtime stream.

pillars.title: Topics & webhooks
pillars.text: Fan out to subscribers with signed, retried deliveries.

pillars.title: Queues & streams
pillars.text: Competing consumers with leases, and ordered history with cursors.

pillars.title: Realtime
pillars.text: Server-sent events to browsers, resuming where they left off.

pillars.title: Replay & DLQ
pillars.text: Nothing is lost quietly: replay it, or inspect what failed.

faq.question: What is OpenVibe.Events?
faq.answer: The event system every OpenVibe product publishes through: durable events, topics and subscriptions, signed webhooks with retries, dead-letter queues with replay, and a realtime stream for browsers.

faq.question: Can my own app use it?
faq.answer: Yes. With a project on OpenVibe.Services, an app token publishes your app's events, reads them with a cursor and subscribes webhooks to them.

faq.question: What if my webhook is down?
faq.answer: Deliveries are signed and retried. One that still fails goes to a dead-letter queue, where it can be inspected and replayed, so nothing is dropped quietly.

faq.question: How do browsers get live updates?
faq.answer: Server-sent events at openvibe.events/realtime/stream, which pick up from a cursor after a dropped connection.

keywords: event bus api, webhook retry service, sqs alternative, sns alternative, pub sub api, realtime sse api, dead letter queue, webhook replay
